data.name: Vampire: The Masquerade® - Bloodlines™ 2
data.detailed_description:
Editions


Acerca do jogo

Combate na pele de um vampiro antigo numa Seattle moderna à beira de uma guerra aberta. Conhece as figuras mais poderosas, escolhe os teus aliados e decide quem ficará no poder e qual será o destino da cidade.

Um cerco de três frentes a Seattle, um vácuo de poder na corte vampírica e o despertar de um vampiro antigo em conflito com a voz na sua cabeça, concretizados pelo estúdio The Chinese Room, vencedor do prémio BAFTA.

Tu és o monstro

O sangue sustenta-te e alimenta as tuas disciplinas vampíricas. Vais perseguir e alimentar-te da população da cidade à noite. Usa os teus poderes sobrenaturais ou a tua capacidade de persuasão pura nos civis para os atraíres para becos escuros onde poderás saciar a tua fome. Cuidado, não violes as regras do Baile de Máscaras: evita revelar a tua natureza ou arriscas-te a sofrer represálias — primeiro da polícia e depois... bem, lembra-te de que não és a única criatura da noite.

Explora um sistema de combate visceral e imersivo que recompensa abordagens e estilos de jogo completamente diferentes com base no clã de vampiros que escolhes. Vais lutar com socos sobrenaturais, recorrer às tuas capacidades de persuasão ou levar a melhor atacando cada presa uma a uma como o superpredador que és? A escolha do clã permite estes estilos de jogo e não só.

World of Darkness

Entra no World of Darkness e ascende na hierarquia da sociedade vampírica ou revolta-te contra ela. Descobre Seattle, uma cidade repleta de personagens e fações perigosas e fascinantes, para não mencionar os mortais em jogo no conflito de poderes sobre o qual nada sabem. Nesta sequela do clássico de culto, as tuas escolhas, planos e esquemas vão determinar o equilíbrio de poderes e o que acontece à cidade e aos seus habitantes.

reviews.review:
Questionable Choices

As a 30 years long time fan of Vampire the Masquerade, and a day one player of Bloodlines 1 (CD-ROM no less!),  I will give a brief review followed by a more in-depth one for those who are Kindred Curious. 

The TL;DR? The game has a few pro's, MANY con's and as the review started out, questionable choices. If you are a fan of VtM, this is a decent game so long as you go in with an open mind BUT get it at a discount as it's many flaws hold it back from being something truly fangtastic.

Pros: 
- Visually stunning environmental details; Snowy Seattle looks amazing
- Solid Voice acting (mostly)
- Lighting and Sound are delicious
- Soundtrack and overall vibe hits the World of Darkness feels
- Variety of abilities leads to several pathways to solve combat
- Resonance system enhances feel of street level predator
- Outfits affecting resonance is a cool idea

Cons:
- Facial/body animations are stilted and sometimes out of place
- The name Phyre for a 300 year old elder is a terrible choice
- Some over acting breaks immersion
- Irregular difficulty spikes
- Too Heavy an Emphasis on Combat
- Some game breaking glitches
- Half baked masquerade system
- many of the outfits are lackluster or belong on a Parisian fashion-show cat walk

Ah, What could have been...First and foremost, the name Phyre is a truly terrible choice in character naming. A 300 year old Near-East kindred wakes up and decides they will name themselves after a band poster which phonetically sounds like a Kindred's greatest fear and NO other Kindred question it? The Nomad (i.e. phyre) is the worst offender of the masquerade: waking from torpor and throughout the game, the nomad goes on a city wide slaughter-fest of anarchs, thin bloods, ghouls and other entities that makes little sense. The amount of bodies and/or missing persons left in their wake would surely draw the SI, First Light and Society of St Leopold in a heartbeat. 

The masquerade system makes absolutely no sense. If i glide down from a 10 story rooftop and plunk right down next to the police, barely a glance is cast my way, but if I am sprinting (not vampiric dashing mind you) and I hurdle the hood of a car, THAT will raise the cops ire? A questionable design decision: We get staked from behind if the masquerade is breached and we remain on street level; Flee to the rooftops and wait out the breach and you're fine? I would rather have seen more hunters of any variety on the streets that followed and stalked us. It's possible, with how the different Resonant NPCs will follow or flee from you depending on your interaction with them.

The biggest positive for me was Seattle itself. Never has a VtM game looked this gorgeous: The Chinese Room really knocked it out of the park with a snowy Seattle setting that made me want to keep playing the game and hunting resonances until we Cainites were Beckoned home. Some comical moments with the police involve those of Chloleric resonance chasing me and a police officer immediately opens fire (Phyre?) on the aggressively hapless mortal. bang bang, time to go hunting that resonance again

The Abilities/Disciplines terminology are another unusual decision: Newbies to the world of darkness won't notice  the questionable naming conventions but to anyone familiar with the Table top game it's head scratching: The names "unseen aura" and "unseen passage" should have their names flipped; blood salvo is a questionable Thaumaturgy skill; Telekinesis only occurs in Thin-bloods in the TT game (or movement of the mind blood sorcery path) and we inherently get 1 dot in Auspex for all clans (heightened senses) probably from Diablerie off the bat. To those unfamiliar with VtM in any edition, these may sound like (or may be) petty gripes, but they are legit complaints none the less. Video games should synergize with their source material instead of deviating this far off the mark. 

While on the subject of disciplines i must say there are some lovely choices to be made with combat: using cauldron of blood/approach gathered enemies/mass manipulation/terminal decree can eliminate large-ish groups of enemies and its very satisfying watching them all unalive themselves. By far that was my favorite  ability combination playing as a Tremere on my first playthrough

Voice acting is rather solid, with a few caveats. Fabien is entertaining although sometimes his noir-detective schtick is over done and breaks immersion as "the monster" you should be at all times. Hearing the legendary Jason Carl on the radio had me hoping to hear more of his weather reports, alas it is a one and done broadcast. Huddy does a pretty great job as BET of Night and the progression of her radio program compelled  me to hang around the radio to hear them it out in their entirety. Tolly though has way too much snark for my liking and frankly, I can see why a Nosferatu would have turned his arrogant ass into a Kindred. Niko, Fletcher and Patience are also decently fleshed out characters although the pronunciation of "Tzimisce" would have any fiend go into an immediate frenzy and flay the auditory offender

The difficulty spikes (looking at you Seattle Underground) forced me to turn the difficulty way down. Without giving away spoilers, some of the enemies below Seattle deal massive damage, swarm you in a zerg-like fashion and you can't easily replenish your abilities. BEST TIP: zoom in like you're going to use an ability and use that time slowdown to aim for headshots or time your weapon swings to handle crowd control, let off the zoom, activate it again...rinse and repeat. The IAO (i.e. hunters) can be managed in the same manner coupled with Heightened senses to see through their flashbangs and underground darkness. 

I had difficulty determining what the cumulative effect of "Person X was displeased/annoyed/irritated" dialogue had on the game. Mostly I sided with the Camarilla court but in the end i somehow immediately flipped to Anarch? After slaughtering their ghouls wholesale throughout most of the game? The lack of RPG mechanics for dialogue in the game made navigating the conversations a frustrating and unrewarding endeavor

The intrigue within the story itself is tantalizing and TCR did a good job of weaving a narrative that kept my attention and wanting more. The storyline and Seattle itself kept my attention long enough to overlook the aforementioned complaints and finish the game. All in all, I took my time soaking in the gameplay elements I enjoyed and finished the main story in 40 hours. Finding the anarch graffiti and camera locations was quite tedious and while i got close, I chose to finish the main storyline instead of wrapping up these side quests.

On a final note, I place the several gripes I have squarely in the lap of Paradox Interactive. I remember the teasers that we saw from the game's initial reveal and muse over what might have been. The video snippets of the various clans, the storyline of being a thin blood and then being able to pick a clan through Court sanctioned diablerie, chasing Slugg through "The Jungle" and the subsequent dialogue choices to determine his fate...all of it scrapped except for some elements of the environmental design. Whoever made the decision to axe the initial path of the game did a great disservice to the fans of VtM. The outrage over 2 clans being locked behind a pay wall and the middling "Santa monica cosmetic pack" was justified. That scenario was insulting enough that it diminished my enthusiasm to the point of not purchasing the game for a year and even now after the QoL updates (fabien's fast travel, being able to hold weapons) I still lament over what could have been.

I decided to give the game a recommend status but I am 50/50 on whether to recommend. Get the game at a deep discount and I'm sure you'll be able to overlook similar complaints and enjoy your time hunting and haunting the streets of Seattle
